findings.title: Figures 1 and 3 have no generating script in the repository
findings.quote: Results for each application can be reproduced by running the files reproduce_[X].m, where [X] = Gauss, Liu, KEF, EGM.
findings.claim: The repo provides reproduce_*.m for the four applications (Figs 2,4,5,6) plus the Ising example (Fig. D.5) and aux_reproduce_results_Gauss.m for appendix figures, but nothing computes Figure 1 (KSD² insensitivity to mixture proportion, Eq. 11) or Figure 3 (the posterior influence function). A repo-wide grep for 'influence', 'PIF', or the mixture found no such code.
findings.concern: Two numbered figures in the main text cannot be regenerated from the repository, so their values are not independently checkable.
findings.resolution: Authors: please add (or point to) the scripts that produce Figure 1 and Figure 3, or state that these figures are illustrative and out of reproduction scope.

findings.title: M_Liu robust preconditioner derivative uses the wrong denominator in rows 3-5
findings.claim: out.mx is meant to be the Jacobian d(m_i)/d(x_j) of the weighting vector out.m defined two lines above (out.m(3)=(1+x1^2+x3^2)^-1/2, out.m(4)=(1+x1^2+x4^2)^-1/2, out.m(5)=(1+x1^2+x5^2)^-1/2). Rows 3,4,5 of out.mx instead all use the denominator (1+x1^2+x2^2)^-3/2, i.e. the x2 term where x3/x4/x5 are required. KSD_Bayes.m (scalar branch, via divx_M) consumes diag(out.mx), so entries mx(3,3), mx(4,4), mx(5,5) are wrong.
findings.concern: The divergence term of νn (out.vn) for the robust Liu posterior is computed from a preconditioner derivative that is inconsistent with the preconditioner itself, so the robust generalised-posterior mean shown in Figure 4 (right column) is numerically incorrect.
findings.resolution: Replace (1+x1^2+x2^2)^(-3/2) in rows 3-5 with (1+x1^2+x3^2), (1+x1^2+x4^2), (1+x1^2+x5^2) respectively. See _audit_code/check_M_Liu_gradient.py: diag(coded mx) disagrees with the finite-difference Jacobian of out.m by up to ~1.9 on rows 3-5 while rows 1-2 and the corrected version agree to ~1e-10.
findings.paper_ref: §6.2 robust weighting function M(x); Figure 4 right column

findings.title: Liu standard-Bayes normaliser mis-scales the Gauss-Hermite rule; C(0,0)=0.47, not 1
findings.claim: C(t1,t2) is meant to approximate the intractable normaliser Cθ = E_{(x4,x5)~N(0,Sig_45)}[exp(t1*tanh(x4)+t2*tanh(x5))] (paper §6.2 footnote 6). The Gauss-Hermite nodes (roots for the exp(-x^2) weight) are mapped by `nodes_2D * Sig_45_chol` WITHOUT the sqrt(2) scaling the Gaussian change-of-variables requires, the weight constant is (2*pi)^-1 instead of pi^-1, and an extra det(Sig_45_chol)^-1 factor is applied.
findings.concern: The cubature does not integrate to 1 for the constant function (a hard requirement for a probability-measure expectation): _audit_code/check_liu_cubature.py replicates the code exactly and gets C(0,0)=0.4655 versus the textbook GH rule and Monte-Carlo which both give 1.0000; the error is (t1,t2)-dependent (ratio drifts 0.47→0.37), so the -n*log C(t1,t2) term distorts the SHAPE of the standard-Bayes posterior shown in Figure 4 (left column), not merely its scale.
findings.resolution: Use x = sqrt(2)*L*z with weights pi^-1 * w_i * w_j and no det factor (or an equivalent correctly-normalised 2D Gaussian GH rule). Check that C(0,0)=1. See _audit_code/check_liu_cubature.py.
findings.paper_ref: §6.2 footnote 6 (Gauss-Hermite cubature of order 10); Figure 4 left column

findings.title: Gauss Figure-2 bottom row uses uncapped out.w, omitting the min(1,·) of Eq. (15)
findings.claim: Eq. (15) and §6 ('the default settings of Section 5 were used' for all experiments) prescribe β = min(1, βn), where βn = out.w. The second loop of this script (displacement experiment, Figure 2 bottom row; lines 118 and 126 for the non-robust and robust posteriors) multiplies out.An/out.vn by the raw out.w, omitting the min(1,·) cap. The first loop (lines 37-38, 46-47) and every other reproduce_results_*.m apply min(1,out.w) — see _audit_code/check_beta_min_consistency.py, which finds these two sites are the only uncapped ones of ten.
findings.concern: The bottom-row panels of Figure 2 are computed with a different β rule than the top-row panels and than the paper's stated default, so if βn>1 for that data they are over-shrunk relative to the method as described.
findings.resolution: Wrap out.w in min(1,·) in the second loop for consistency with Eq. (15) and the rest of the codebase; or confirm the cap does not bind for this data (βn<=1, in which case the panels are unaffected).
